title: Relative global complete-intersection equations are Koszul-regular
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n,c\geq0$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose the specified presentation $P/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Then $H_i(K_\bullet(P;f_1,\ldots,f_c))=0$ for every $i>0$; that is, $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Empty sequences and the zero quotient are allowed, with no Noetherian assumption on $R$.

proof.text: Put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and $K=K_\bullet(P;f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. The differential formula of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] gives $d(e_j\wedge z)=f_jz-e_j\wedge dz$. Thus if $dz=0$, $f_jz=d(e_j\wedge z)$ is a boundary. Every generator $f_j$ therefore annihilates every homology class, and so $I H_i(K)=0$. This is the explicit calculation of Tag 0663, not an extra lemma.

Fix a prime $\mathfrak Q\subset P$ containing $I$. The ideal $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak Q/I$ in $P/I$ is prime: a product of residue classes belongs to it exactly when a product of representatives belongs to $\mathfrak Q$. Its inverse image is $\mathfrak Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] to this prime and the specified presentation. It gives regularity of $f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1$ in $P_{\mathfrak Q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], their Koszul homology vanishes in every positive degree. Neither result assumes that $R$ is Noetherian.

For any prime $\mathfrak Q\subset P$, localize the complex at $T=P\setminus\mathfrak Q$. Exactness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies localized cycles with the kernel of the localized differential and localized boundaries with its image; applying it also to $0\to\operatorname{im}d_{i+1}\to\ker d_i\to H_i(K)\to0$ identifies $H_i(K)_{\mathfrak Q}$ with $H_i(T^{-1}K)$. By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso], $T^{-1}K$ is the Koszul complex of $f_j/1$ over $P_{\mathfrak Q}$: on each standard wedge basis, the scalar-extension identification sends $a/s$ times a wedge to that same wedge with coefficient $a/s$. Hence Step 2 gives $H_i(K)_{\mathfrak Q}=0$ for $i>0$ whenever $I\subseteq\mathfrak Q$.

If $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak Q$, some $f_j\notin\mathfrak Q$. Step 1 says that $f_j$ kills $H_i(K)$, hence also every fraction in $H_i(K)_{\mathfrak Q}$. But $f_j$ acts bijectively on this localization by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], since $f_j\in P\setminus\mathfrak Q$. Consequently this localized module is zero. This also handles the unit-ideal case $P/I=0$.

Fix $i>0$. Steps 3 and 4 give $H_i(K)_{\mathfrak m}=0$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to the map $0\to H_i(K)$. Each localized map is bijective, so this map is bijective and $H_i(K)=0$. Since the complex has zero terms in negative degrees, its negative homology is zero too. This is precisely Koszul-regularity by [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. For $c=0$, $K$ is simply $P$ in degree zero, so the same conclusion holds.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q108-024d2d9eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: five steps, no new nodes. The item statement is identical to live and matches Stacks 07D2 (more-algebra.tex l.8386): the given presentation, arbitrary R, no Noetherian assumption. The item is still unsplit on live and side-live, so no other group superseded it. Step 1: the formula D(v∧x)=φ(v)x−v∧Dx from def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex gives f_j z=d(e_j∧z), so (f) kills H_i. This is a correct elementary step; lem-k3-koszul-generator-homotopy could be cited (advisory). Step 2: forms q=Q/I with inverse image Q, then applies 00SV(1) (local-regular-sequence node, same hypotheses) and 062F (needs only injectivity, no Noetherian). Step 3: localization exactness (00CS) gives H_i(K)_Q=H_i(T⁻¹K); lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso (whole complexes, any algebra) identifies T⁻¹K with K_{P_Q}(f/1). Step 4: an f_j outside Q both kills the localized homology and acts bijectively on it, so it is 0; this also covers S=0. Step 5: 00HN(6) applied to 0→H_i, plus negative degrees vanish, gives Koszul-regular exactly as defined. Edge cases c=0, c>n, a unit f_j, R=0 and non-Noetherian R all hold. Grepping 07D2, 0663 and relative-global-CI+Koszul found no duplicate; main-20261015 has no statement of this item. No SGA. I accept the three tool_uses (00SV, 062F, Koszul base change): all generic algebra that 07D2 needs. The inherited from.node=null is a base-node matter. No fixes.
